pages.text: The World Shard Miner uses the beacon's complete same-block base: Diamond Blocks select Overworld, Ancient Debris selects Nether, and Purpur Blocks select the End. Levels one through four increase work rate, and the structure can activate in any dimension.

The three built-in modes select ores by target dimension/biome. By default it scans the final server world's live ore-generation rules, so datapacks and other mods participate; data/*/world_shard_miner/*.json can define or override modes.

Inside the exact owner's personal realm, output is committed directly to that owner's storage. Elsewhere, the miner uses its own 27-slot cache and reports Cache Full when blocked. An unavailable owner realm pauses realm output and resumes after the cache/storage condition clears.

The Treasure Basin only observes an active World Shard Miner directly below to choose its loot mode; the blocks never communicate. It inherits only the mode and immutable owner snapshot, owns a separate 27-slot cache and status, and can block the beacon beam.

Every 2400 ticks the basin generates one loot cycle from the current server LootTable and the owner's luck. Data packs can add or override mode-selected loot definitions under data/*/world_shard_loot/*.json. Missing selectable loot reports CALIBRATING instead of generating an empty drop.

Miner and basin caches, full pauses and Xianqiao-unavailable states are independent. Owner-realm output uses an all-or-nothing storage transaction; non-realm output is published only to that machine's cache, so a rejected cycle cannot lose or contaminate the other machine's state.
